identity.title: Combatting Dimensional Collapse in LLM Pre-Training Data via Submodular File Selection

problem.claim: Select high-quality LLM pre-training files under limited computation while preserving broad performance and efficiency.

gap.claim: Existing proxy-based domain-similarity selection can cause feature-space dimensional collapse: domain-task gains accompany severe generic-performance degradation.

contributions.claim: DiSF selects decorrelated text files in feature space to improve diversity.
The method uses greedy selection to make selected-text covariance eigenvalues more uniform and analyzes approximation under a γ-weakly submodular formulation.
The authors establish a benchmark and evaluate DiSF on TinyLlama models ranging from 120M to 1.1B parameters across nine Harness tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present diversified, decorrelation-based file selection as a way to combat dimensional collapse in LLM pre-training data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant overall-performance improvement across nine Harness tasks.

The authors report that DiSF retains 1.5% of SlimPajama’s 590M files, outperforms full-data pre-training within a 50B training budget, and achieves about 1.5× training efficiency and 5× data efficiency.
The authors report that the method is supported by an approximation analysis for a γ-weakly submodular optimization formulation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Limited computation makes quality-focused pre-training data selection important.
Proxy models commonly select files by similarity to a target domain, but this can collapse feature-space diversity and harm generic performance.
DiSF selects decorrelated files using greedy optimization aimed at more uniform covariance eigenvalues.
The authors benchmark DiSF on TinyLlama models and nine Harness tasks, reporting broad gains and strong efficiency numbers.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific failure mode—dimensional collapse—to a measurable selection objective based on decorrelation and covariance eigenvalues.

lessons.interpretation: Naming the failure mode and aligning it with an explicit optimization target makes the method’s rationale testable.
lessons.application: Frame a data-selection method by first identifying the representation pathology it addresses, then define a selection objective that directly measures or counteracts that pathology.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the target domain is intentionally narrow or when representation diversity conflicts with the task objective.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide numerical baselines, uncertainty, task-wise results, or experimental settings supporting the reported improvements.
The exact approximation guarantee, γ value, feature representation, and compute/data-efficiency accounting are unspecified.
The reported results cover TinyLlama and SlimPajama; broader architectures, datasets, and budgets are not established here.
